name: The Tolman household at 2031 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_tolman_samuel_a

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2031 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2031 Mr. & Mrs. Samuel A. Tolman.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2031, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The two live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Samuel A. Tolman
persons.note: The 1900 census lists S. A. Tolman here as head, born March 1837, in Maine, married, wholesale grain (ED 40, sheet 12B, line 69, leaf n817).

persons.name: Mrs. Samuel A. Tolman
persons.note: The 1900 census lists Bessie Tolman here as wife, born August 1849 (the figures are hard to read), in New Hampshire, married (ED 40, sheet 12B, line 70, leaf n817).

persons.name: Ida Nelson

born.note: The census gives October 1862, age 37 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "House maid" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the house, as a servant (house maid); born October 1862 (the figures are hard to read), in Sweden, came to the United States in 1888, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the rear building behind the house, as the head of his own household there (coachman); born February 1862, in England, married. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.
